harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s reconciliation job with an exclusive, non-blocking kernel file lock. Concurrent runs now exit 75 with a clear message, duplicate batches are prevented, interrupted runs release ownership automatically, and the change persisted through reboot.
actions_performed: Added whole-job locking using the installed legacy-compatible flock 2.13.
Used exact fixed-line matching for batch IDs.
Preserved B100 and processed B101/B102 exactly once.
Verified concurrent invocation and interruption recovery.
Restarted node1 and confirmed configuration and data recovery without changing Ubuntu 7.10 or kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.

evidence.requirement: Only one invocation processes pending.tsv at a time, with a clear contention result
evidence.summary: Installed non-blocking exclusive locking; contenders returned exit 75 with “another invocation already owns the job”.

evidence.requirement: Each batch ID reaches ledger.tsv once and existing entries are preserved
evidence.summary: B100 remained intact; B101 and B102 each occur once. Concurrent duplicate-input testing produced exactly one ledger entry per ID.

evidence.requirement: An interrupted invocation does not permanently block later work
evidence.summary: A lock-owning invocation was terminated with status 143; the following invocation immediately succeeded and recorded its batch exactly once.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were confirmed before and after restart.

Baseline boot ID was 0ab8f0a8-0074-4c8b-8034-d4e3d42f9001; restart was acknowledged; recovered boot ID was 25c45d20-522f-4cec-84eb-414c7ee59dbd. The script, network identity, lock availability, and B100/B101/B102 ledger data recovered, and a post-restart reconciliation left the ledger checksum unchanged.
